questions.stem: Many banyan trees have thick roots that grow from their branches towards the ground. What are these roots called?
options: Climbing stems
Flower stalks
Storage roots
Aerial roots

explain.why: Climbing stems are stems that wind around a support. These are roots, not stems.
Flower stalks hold up flowers. These hanging parts are roots.
Storage roots are thick roots under the ground, like a carrot, that store food.

solution: Roots that grow in the air are called aerial roots.

figure.alt: A banyan tree with a thick trunk, spreading branches and roots hanging from the branches.

questions.stem: A banyan tree has thick roots hanging from its branches (part B). How do these roots help the tree?
options: They attract insects to the flowers of the tree
They reach the ground and help to hold up the very heavy tree
They protect the seeds as they grow in the fruit
They make food for the whole tree using light and water

explain.why: Insects are attracted by the flowers, not by the roots.
Protecting seeds is the job of the fruit.
Food is made by the leaves (part C), not by the roots.

solution: Aerial roots that grow down into the ground help to support a large tree.

figure.alt: A banyan tree in line art with a thick trunk, spreading branches with leaves, and long roots hanging down from the branches, with four marked positions.

questions.stem: An orchid grows on the trunk of a tree. The roots labelled B hang in the air. Which statement about them is correct?
options: They hold up the leaves so they get sunlight
They grip the tree and take in moisture from the air
They take in water and mineral salts from the soil below the tree
They make the seeds that grow into new orchids

explain.why: Holding leaves up is a job of stems. These roots grip the tree.
The orchid sits on the trunk, not in soil. Its aerial roots take in moisture from the air.
Seeds are made by flowers, not by roots.

solution: Orchid aerial roots cling to the tree and take in moisture from the air.

figure.alt: An orchid growing on a tree trunk in line art, with a flower, leaves and long roots hanging in the air, with four marked positions.

questions.stem: A money plant has a weak stem. Small roots (part C) on its stem press against a pole. How does this help the plant?
options: The flowers of the plant open later in the night
The stem is held on the pole so the leaves can reach more light
The fruits grow larger on the plant and fall off sooner
The plant no longer needs its leaves to make food

explain.why: The small roots hold the stem on the pole. They do not change when flowers open.
The roots on the stem grip the pole. They do not make fruits larger.
All green plants still need leaves to make food.

solution: The small roots grip the pole so the weak stem climbs up towards the light.

figure.alt: A money plant climbing up a pole in line art, with heart-shaped leaves, a weak stem and small roots on the stem pressed against the pole, with four marked positions.

questions.stem: A pea plant has a weak stem. Its tendrils (part A) curl round a support. How does this help the plant?
options: The tendrils take in water from the moist air
The stem is held up so the leaves get light
The tendrils keep animals away from the plant
The tendrils make the seeds for the whole plant

explain.why: Tendrils hold on to a support. Water is taken in by the roots.
Keeping animals away is the job of thorns, not tendrils.
Seeds are made by the flower (part D), not the tendrils.

solution: Tendrils wind round a support and help the weak stem to climb.

figure.alt: A pea plant with a thin stem climbing a support in line art, with leaves, a flower and curly thread-like parts wound round the support, with four marked positions.

questions.stem: A cactus grows in a dry desert. How does the thick stem (part B) help it to live there?
options: It stores water for the dry times
It makes more leaves to lose water quickly
It attracts insects to the flowers
It lets the cactus float on water

explain.why: A cactus has spines, not leaves, so that it loses very little water.
Insects are attracted by the flower (part D), not by the stem.
A cactus does not live in water; its thick stem is a water store.

solution: The thick stem of a cactus holds water the plant can use when there is no rain.

figure.alt: A cactus in the desert in line art, shallow spreading roots and a flower, with four marked positions.

questions.stem: The stalk of a water lily (part B) has many air spaces. How does this help the plant?
options: It takes in more mineral salts from the mud below
It helps the leaf float to get sunlight
It stores seeds for when the pond dries up
It attracts more insects to the flower

explain.why: Mineral salts are taken in by the roots (part C) in the mud, not by the stalk.
The stalk does not store seeds. Its air spaces help the plant float.
Insects are attracted by the flower (part D), not by air spaces in the stalk.

solution: Air spaces make the stalk and leaf float so the leaf can get sunlight.

figure.alt: A water lily in a pond in line art, with a wide leaf floating on the surface, a long stalk, a flower and roots in the mud, with four marked positions.

questions.stem: Mangrove trees grow in soft mud. How do the thick, arching roots labelled B help the tree?
options: They hold the tree up firmly in mud
They take in air from the water around them
They carry the seeds of the tree to the mud
They make food for the tree

explain.why: The roots that stick up out of the mud (part A) help the tree get air. These arching roots hold it up.
Roots do not carry seeds. These roots hold the tree in the mud.
Food is made by the leaves (part C).

solution: Roots arching from the trunk spread out and hold the tree up in soft mud.

figure.alt: A mangrove tree in muddy water in line art, with curved roots arching from the trunk into the mud, short roots sticking up out of the mud, leaves and a trunk, with four marked positions.

questions.stem: Mangrove mud has very little air. Some roots (part A) grow upwards out of the mud. How does this help the tree?
options: They stop the tree from floating away
They let the roots get air
They attract insects to the flowers
They take in more sunlight for making food

explain.why: Holding the tree down is done by the arching roots (part B), not the roots sticking up.
Insects are attracted by flowers, not by roots.
Making food is done by the leaves (part C). Roots do not make food.

solution: Roots that stick up out of the mud take in air for the roots below.

figure.alt: A mangrove tree in muddy water in line art, with curved roots arching from the trunk into the mud, short roots sticking up out of the mud, leaves and a trunk, with four marked positions.

questions.stem: The thick orange part of a carrot is a root that stores food. Why is this useful to the carrot plant?
options: It lets the plant float on water
It protects the seeds of the carrot
It makes food for the plant using the sunlight under the soil
The plant can use the stored food later to grow

explain.why: A carrot plant grows in soil and a storage root does not help it float.
Seeds are protected by fruits. The carrot root holds food.
There is no sunlight under the soil, so it cannot make food there.

solution: A storage root keeps food that the plant can use later.

questions.stem: Kangkong grows floating in ponds. How does its hollow stem (part B) help it?
options: The hollow stem makes food for the roots below
The hollow stem takes in water from the pond
The water inside the stem makes the plant sink down
The air inside helps it to float

explain.why: Food is made by the leaves (part A).
Water is taken in by the roots (part C).
The air in the hollow stem makes the plant float, not sink.

solution: A hollow stem is full of air, which helps the kangkong float.

figure.alt: A kangkong plant floating in water in line art, with leaves, a long hollow stem and roots hanging in the water, with three marked positions.

questions.stem: Which feature best helps a plant to live in a very dry place?
options: A thick stem that stores water, and sharp spines
Long roots that hang in the air
Hollow stems full of air
Wide, thin leaves with a great many stomata

explain.why: Hanging aerial roots take moisture from damp air and would not help in a dry place.
Hollow stems full of air help plants float in water, not live in dry places.
Wide leaves with many stomata would lose too much water in a dry place.

solution: A plant in a dry place needs to save water.
A thick stem stores water. Spines lose very little.

questions.stem: A plant on the dark floor of a rainforest has large, thin leaves. How does this help it?
options: The leaves can catch more of the weak light
The leaves can lose less water vapour to the air
The leaves can hold the plant in the soil
The leaves can store more water

explain.why: A large, thin leaf has more surface and so loses more water, not less.
Holding the plant in the soil is done by the roots.
Thin leaves cannot store much water.

solution: A large leaf surface catches more of the weak light.

questions.stem: A tree on a windy seashore has strong roots that spread wide and deep. How does this help the tree?
options: The roots grip the soil so wind cannot blow it over
The roots help the leaves to float in the air above the tree
The roots attract insects to the flowers
The roots make food from the sunlight

explain.why: Leaves do not float in the air, and roots do not lift them.
Insects are attracted by flowers, not by roots.
Food is made by the leaves. Roots get no sunlight.

solution: Strong, spreading roots hold the tree firmly so it is not blown over.

questions.stem: Which statement is true of both the hanging roots of a banyan tree and the aerial roots of an orchid?
options: They hold the plant in the soil under it
They make the seeds of the plant
They make food using sunlight
They grow out in the air, above the ground

explain.why: An orchid on a tree trunk does not grow in soil.
Seeds are made by flowers.
Food is made mainly by leaves, not by these roots.

solution: Aerial roots grow in the air.
Banyan roots hang from the branches and orchid roots hang from the tree they grow on.

questions.stem: A cactus grows in a hot, dry desert. Which part of the cactus stores water?
options: The thick stem
The tiny roots only
The flowers
The sharp spines

explain.why: Roots take water in. The water is stored in the thick stem.
Flowers help the plant to make seeds, not store water.
Spines are thin and cannot hold water.

solution: The thick stem of a cactus stores water for the dry times.

figure.alt: A cactus growing in the desert.

questions.stem: The leaves of a cactus are thin, sharp spines. How does this help the cactus live in a desert?
options: It takes in more water from the air
Less water is lost from the plant
It makes the stem grow taller
More light is caught for making food

explain.why: Spines do not take in water.
Spines have nothing to do with height.
Wide leaves, not spines, catch more light.

solution: Small spines have very little surface, so very little water vapour escapes.

figure.alt: A cactus growing in the desert.

questions.stem: Some roots of a mangrove tree grow upwards out of the muddy water. Why does the tree have these roots?
options: To make seeds
To catch sunlight
To take in air
To take in more mud

explain.why: Seeds are not made in roots.
Roots do not catch light. Leaves do.
The tree does not need to take in mud.

solution: Mud has very little air. Roots growing up into the air can take it in.

figure.alt: A mangrove tree in muddy water, with curved roots arching from the trunk and some roots growing up out of the mud.

questions.stem: A water lily has wide leaves that float on the water. How does this help the plant?
options: The leaves can take in water from the soil
The leaves can catch lots of sunlight
The leaves can hold the plant in the mud
The leaves can store air for the roots

explain.why: Leaves are not the part that takes in water from the soil.
Roots hold a plant in the mud, not floating leaves.
Storing air is not the job of wide leaves.

solution: Floating leaves lie in the light, so they can make food.

figure.alt: A water lily in a pond, with a wide leaf floating on the surface.

questions.stem: A fish has a smooth body that is narrow at the front and the back. How does this help the fish?
options: It can move through water easily
It can hide among rocks on land
It can breathe air easily
It can stay on land for a long time

explain.why: A fish lives in water, so this does not help.
A fish breathes with its gills. Its shape does not help it breathe air.
A fish cannot live on land.

solution: A smooth, narrow body makes less push from the water, so the fish swims fast.

questions.stem: A camel has a hump that stores fat. How does this help the camel in the desert?
options: It stops the camel from sweating
It helps the camel to float
It is a store of food for hard times
It keeps the camel cool in the shade

explain.why: The fat does not stop sweating.
A camel does not live in water.
The hump is a food store, not a cooler.

solution: Fat in the hump can be used as food when there is little to eat.

questions.stem: A polar bear has thick fur and a thick layer of fat under its skin. How does this help it?
options: It keeps the bear warm in the cold
It helps the bear to hide in the desert
It helps the bear to run fast
It lets the bear store water

explain.why: Polar bears live in cold places, not deserts.
Fur and fat do not make it faster.
Fat and fur keep in heat. They are not for storing water.

solution: Thick fur and fat keep heat in, so the bear stays warm.

questions.stem: A tortoise pulls its head and legs into its hard shell when it is in danger. How does the shell help it?
options: It keeps the tortoise cool in the sun
It helps the tortoise to swim fast
It helps the tortoise to find food
It protects the tortoise from enemies

explain.why: The shell is for protection.
A heavy shell does not make it swim fast.
A shell does not help find food.

solution: A hard shell is hard for enemies to bite or crush, so the tortoise is safer.

questions.stem: A duck has webbed feet. How do they help the duck?
options: They help the duck to dig for worms
They help the duck to climb trees
They push the water to help it swim
They keep the duck warm in the nest

explain.why: Webbed feet are for swimming, not digging.
Webbed feet are not good for climbing.
Webbing on the feet is for swimming.

solution: The skin between the toes makes the foot wide, so it pushes more water.

questions.stem: Many birds fly to a warmer place when the cold season begins. What kind of adaptation is this?
options: A structural adaptation
A behavioural adaptation
A food-making adaptation
A seed dispersal adaptation

explain.why: A structural adaptation is a body part. Flying away is an action the bird does.
The birds do not make food. They move to find food and warmth.
Seed dispersal is about plants. Birds are moving themselves.

solution: Moving to another place is something the animal does, so it is behavioural.

questions.stem: Which of these is a structural adaptation?
options: A porcupine's sharp quills
A bird flying to a warmer place
A bear sleeping through the cold season
A squirrel storing nuts

explain.why: This is something the bird does, so it is behavioural.
This is behaviour, not a body part.
This is behaviour, not a body part.

solution: A structural adaptation is a part of the body, such as quills.
The other three are things animals do.

questions.stem: A seed has a thin, light wing. How does the wing help the plant?
options: It helps the seed to take in water
It helps the seed to float on a pond
It sticks the seed to an animal's fur
The wind can carry the seed far away

explain.why: The wing is not for taking in water.
The thin wing is for the wind, not water.
Sticking to fur needs hooks or sticky parts, not a wing.

solution: A light wing catches the wind, so seeds travel away from the parent plant.

questions.stem: A coconut has a thick husk that holds air. How does this help the coconut plant?
options: It lets the wind carry the coconut
It can float to faraway places
It makes animals eat the coconut
It keeps the coconut warm

explain.why: A coconut is too heavy to be carried by wind.
The husk is not a food for animals.
The husk is for floating.

solution: The husk holds air and floats, so water carries the coconut away from the tree.

questions.stem: A seed has many tiny hooks on its outside. How does this help the plant?
options: It can be blown by the wind
It can cling to an animal
It can make food for the plant
It can float on water

explain.why: Hooks do not help a seed travel by wind.
Hooks do not make food.
Hooks do not help a seed float.

solution: Hooks catch on fur or clothes, so the seed is carried to a new place.

questions.stem: A forest is cut down to build a road. What happens to many of the animals that lived there?
options: They lose their homes
They grow thicker fur
They find more food and shelter
They are not affected

explain.why: Animals cannot change their bodies that quickly.
Fewer trees means less food and shelter.
Their habitat is gone, so they are affected.

solution: Trees give food and shelter. When they are cut down, animals lose their homes.

questions.stem: Which of these actions is good for the environment?
options: Burning rubbish in an open field
Pouring used cooking oil down the drain
Planting new trees in a cleared area
Throwing plastic bags into the sea

explain.why: Burning rubbish puts smoke and harmful gases in the air.
Oil pollutes the water and harms animals and plants.
Plastic harms sea animals and does not break down quickly.

solution: New trees give food and shelter and help to replace what was lost.

questions.stem: Why is it harmful to pour oil into the sea?
options: It makes the sea cooler
It gives sea animals more food
It makes the water cleaner
It harms sea animals and plants

explain.why: Oil does not make the sea cooler.
Oil is not food. It covers and poisons animals.
Oil makes water dirty, not clean.

solution: Oil covers the water. It poisons the animals and plants that live in it.

questions.stem: Recycling paper helps the environment because fewer ____ need to be cut down.
options: rocks
clouds
trees
fish

explain.why: Paper is made from trees, not rocks.
Paper is not made from clouds.
Paper is not made from fish.

solution: Paper is made from wood.
Recycling used paper means fewer trees are cut down.

questions.stem: Burning large amounts of fuel puts gases in the air that make the Earth warmer. This is called ____.
options: deforestation
recycling
global warming
reforestation

explain.why: Deforestation is the cutting down of forests.
Recycling means using materials again.
Reforestation means planting trees again.

solution: The Earth getting warmer because of gases from burning fuel is called global warming.

questions.stem: A student brings her own bag when she goes shopping instead of taking new plastic bags. How does this help the environment?
options: More forest is cleared for roads
More trees are cut down
Less plastic rubbish is made
More oil is poured into the sea

explain.why: Her own bag does not clear forests.
A cloth bag does not need more trees to be cut.
This has nothing to do with using her own bag.

solution: Using a bag again means fewer new plastic bags are made and thrown away.

questions.stem: An owl has very large eyes that can see well in dim light. How does this help it?
options: It can hide in the sand
It can store water for a long time
It can hunt at night
It can swim very fast

explain.why: Large eyes do not help an owl hide in sand.
Eyes do not store water.
Eyes do not help an owl swim.

solution: Large eyes let an owl see in the dark, so it can look for food at night.

questions.stem: A frog has green and brown skin that looks like the plants around it. How does this help the frog?
options: It stores food for the frog
It helps the frog swim faster
It keeps the frog warm at night
Enemies find it hard to see the frog

explain.why: Skin colour is not a food store.
Skin colour does not make a frog swim faster.
Skin colour does not keep a frog warm.

solution: Skin that matches the plants helps the frog hide from its enemies.

questions.stem: A mole has strong front legs with large claws. How do they help the mole?
options: It can swim across ponds
It can fly short distances
It can climb tall trees
It can dig tunnels in the soil

explain.why: Strong claws are not for swimming.
A mole cannot fly.
A mole lives under the ground, not in trees.

solution: Strong legs and large claws are good for digging, so a mole can make tunnels.

questions.stem: A giraffe has a very long neck. How does this help it?
options: It can reach leaves high up on trees
It can dig for roots in the ground
It can hide in the long grass
It can swim in deep water

explain.why: A long neck is not for digging.
A tall animal cannot hide easily in grass.
A long neck does not help a giraffe swim.

solution: A long neck lets a giraffe reach food that other animals cannot reach.
